---
name: New Anti-Pattern
about: Submit a templated or generic writing pattern not yet in the catalog (an editorial question, not an AI test)
title: "[PATTERN] "
labels: anti-pattern, contribution
assignees: ''
---

## Pattern name
Give it a short, descriptive name (e.g., "The Recursive Restatement," "The LinkedIn Loop")

## Category
- [ ] Phrase (specific words/phrases to ban or flag)
- [ ] Structure (document-level or section-level pattern)
- [ ] Cadence (a rhythm that hides the point; describe the meaning problem, not a length rule)
- [ ] Fake depth (pseudo-intellectual pattern)
- [ ] Fake authority (unearned credibility pattern)
- [ ] Genre-specific slop (cliché in a specific domain)

## Pattern description
What does it look like? Be specific enough that someone could detect it.

## Example
Show the pattern in action (2-3 sentences minimum).

## Why a reader loses something
What does the reader fail to get when this pattern appears — a checkable fact, a decision, a mechanism, an honest concession? A pattern is an editorial question about the passage; it is never proof that a model or any particular person wrote it, and it is never a trigger for an automatic rewrite. Say who also writes this way (people, templates, models) if you know.

## Detection method
How would you identify this pattern? (Literal phrase, regex, structural description.) Say what a *legitimate* use looks like, so a reviewer can mark it `retain_as_written`.

## Recommended fix
How should it be rewritten? Show a before/after if possible.

## Severity recommendation
- [ ] Hard ban (never use under any circumstances)
- [ ] Soft ban (remove unless it demonstrably earns its place)
- [ ] Earned exception (allowed when intentional and purposeful)

## Where you found it
Did you encounter this in a draft, published writing or your own editing experience? Do not paste text you lack the right to share, and do not cite detector output as the evidence for a pattern.
